name: Cindy Reinert
fact: A resident assistant at Bates-Runner Hall in 1975-76, and a senior from Pewee Valley who had done the job for two years. The Talisman's profile of the resident assistants quotes her saying she disagreed with the rule against drinking in rooms even while enforcing it, and that the hardest part of the job was having to pull up her own friends.

name: Wendell Bratcher
fact: Organizations editor of the 1976 Talisman alongside Maribeth Williams, and a section editor for the first time that year. He is shown cropping pictures and fitting copy for the 26 January deadline, one of the five the book ran to.

name: Howard Sypher
fact: A graduate student from Ft. Lauderdale, Florida. The Talisman's feature on the 1975 summer session quotes him complaining that the university did nothing about entertainment despite rising summer enrolment.

name: Scott Taylor
fact: A member of Pi Kappa Alpha. The fraternity's page in the 1976 Talisman records that he served as its representative to the Associated Student Government, which is the only place in that volume outside the attendance roll where his ASG role is stated.

name: Sherry Casebier
fact: One of the 1975-76 fraternity sweethearts. The Talisman's sweetheart page names her and Patty Campbell as Associated Student Government representatives, and lists her again in the group of sweethearts photographed with Beverly Davenport.

name: Paul Palmer
fact: A member of Lambda Chi Alpha, named in the chapter's membership caption in the 1974 Talisman. This is the only photograph of him the 1973 to 1978 volumes contain, and its rows are too crowded to place him in.

name: Huston Monarch
fact: Indexed in the Talisman as Gilbert Huston Monarch, and a sophomore in 1973-74. The 1974 index is the only volume that gives him a page beyond the ASG attendance roll.

name: Stan McDivitt
fact: A member of Sigma Alpha Epsilon, elected to the Associated Student Government the same year as Steve Henry according to the chapter's page. He also worked in the campus recreation centre, and told the Talisman that Thursday was its busiest night because students went home at weekends.

name: James Keffer
fact: Freshman class president in 1974-75, holding one of the two freshman seats on the Associated Student Government with vice-president Tom Hayes. The Talisman's feature on the class officers notes the pair were one white and one Black, and reports both saying that including class officers in student government was essential. The volume calls him Jay in prose and James Thomas in the class grids.

name: Susan Stuebing
fact: A senior history and economics major from Cincinnati, chosen for the 1973 Who's Who. The entry lists her membership of the Associated Students and its academic council beside the Talisman staff, the student tutorial club, Panhellenic Council and Alpha Delta Pi.

name: Debby Clark
fact: Secretary of the Associated Student Government in 1972-73, one of four executive officers under president Ed Jordan, with Charles Boteler and Mike Fiorella as the two vice presidents and Pat Newton as treasurer. The same page records that the new constitution renamed the body from the Office of Associated Students.

name: Christy Kay Vogt
fact: Freshman class vice-president in 1973-74 with president John Donofrio Jr. The class built a Homecoming float on the theme Camelot as its first project, elected Marcia Heckman as its Homecoming queen candidate, and planned a concert-dance for the spring.
